title: Braided monoidal localization of an ordinary category
statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], and give $\mathcal P$ a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and a braiding $\beta_{P,Q}:P\otimes Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\otimes P$ satisfying the two hexagon identities. Let $W$ be a class of morphisms of $\mathcal P$ containing identities, closed under composition and stable under tensoring on the left and right by every object. Suppose $L:\mathcal P\to\mathcal D$ is a localization at $W$: it sends $W$ to isomorphisms, and for every category $\mathcal E$ precomposition identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal P,\mathcal E)$ of functors sending $W$ to isomorphisms.

Then $\mathcal D$ admits a braided monoidal structure, with tensor denoted $\diamond$ and unit chosen to be $L\mathbf1_{\mathcal P}$, for which $L$ is strong braided monoidal. In particular there are natural isomorphisms $\mu_{P,Q}:LP\diamond LQ\xrightarrow{\sim}L(P\otimes Q)$ and $\mu_0:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\xrightarrow{\sim}L\mathbf1_{\mathcal P}$ obeying the strong monoidal associativity and unit equations and the braided equation
$$L(\beta_{P,Q})\circ\mu_{P,Q}=\mu_{Q,P}\circ\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LP,LQ}.$$
The chosen unit comparison $\mu_0$ is the identity.
